data.source_text_main_point: A Swedish court sentenced four administrators of The Pirate Bay to prison and damages for copyright infringement, but the site's operators claim the verdict is a media stunt and refuse to pay the fines while planning to appeal.

actors.name: The Stockholm district court
variations: a statement released by the court

statements.key_statement: A Swedish court sentenced four TPB administrators to prison and damages for copyright infringement.
statements.long_statement: A Swedish court has sentenced four administrators of the file-sharing site The Pirate Bay to prison terms and ordered them to pay damages for copyright infringement, establishing a legal precedent that the site's operators now intend to challenge through an appeal.

statements.key_statement: A Stockholm district court handed down one-year prison terms to four people for violating copyright rules.
statements.long_statement: Four people were found guilty by the Stockholm district court for helping to break copyright rules. Each person received a one-year prison sentence. Later, the website operators called this verdict a media stunt.

statements.key_statement: TPB operators refuse to shut down the site or pay damages, calling the verdict a media stunt.
statements.long_statement: The operators of The Pirate Bay refuse to shut down the site or halt file sharing operations, characterizing the recent Swedish court verdict as a theater for the media and stating they will not pay the ordered damages.
